text.p: Recently floated Portuguese mobile telephone operator Telecel could boost net profit by between 38 and 58 percent to 9.4-10.4 billion ($60-66 million) escudos next year, according to three analyses conducted by banks.
Telecel-Comunicacoes Pessoais SA is expected to post 1996 net profit of 6.6 to 7.0 billion escudos.

"In 1997 the net result should rise 47 percent to 10.3 billion escudos and, in 1998, this figure should grow by around 23 percent to 13 billion escudos," according to one bank report. The bank asked not to be named.
"Telecel should reach the year 2000 with profits of around 17 billion," it said.
Last year Telecel posted net profit of 2.43 billion escudos.
The analysis said Telecel would start to pay dividends to shareholders on its 1997 results.
"We forecast a 'pay-out' of 45 percent in 1997, which could increase thereafter."
The sale of a 35.6 percent stake in Telecel, which is 51 percent controlled by the European subsidiary of the U.S. AirTouch, was heavily oversubscribed earlier this month.
But the studies warned that increasing competition in the mobile phone market would slow profit growth from 1999.

Rosy forecasts for the domestic mobile phone market have helped boost Telecel's shares from their flotation price of 7,950 escudos to a high of 9,949 escudos. At 1600 GMT on Wednesday, the stock stood at 9,910.
The three analyses forecast earnings per share (EPS) growth of between 172 and 188 percent in 1996, to 316 to 326 escudos.
In 1997 they forecast EPS rising between 43 and 46 percent to 451-478 escudos, with a further gain of some 27 percent to 577 to 601 escudos the following year.
The first study said that the average EPS growth over the three years of some 60 percent compared with a European average for the sector of 20 percent.
One of the studies said that mobile phone penetration would nearly triple by 2000 to 15 percent from some six percent at present, as costs declined and economic growth picked up.
Telecel leads the mobile phone market in Portugal with 51 percent of market share and 60 percent of total sales.
The studies forecast Telecel would generate 1997 sales of between 71 and 74 billion escudos, up from 54 to 58 billion this year.
"In 1998 and 1999, this (sales) growth will slow down to around nine percent and to five percent in the year 2000," the first analysis said.
